cards.title: How Flipping a Retirement Default Doubled Worker Savings
cards.body: In 2001, economists Brigitte Madrian and Dennis Shea revealed the enormous power of inertia in personal finance. When companies required new hires to opt in to a 401(k), only 37% enrolled. But when companies switched to automatic enrollment—requiring workers to actively opt out—participation skyrocketed to 86%. This simple behavioral shift proved so effective that Congress codified automatic enrollment into federal pension law, steering billions into retirement accounts.

sources.title: The Power of Suggestion: Inertia in 401(k) Participation and Savings Behavior

cards.title: How a 1938 Law Invented the Modern 40-Hour Workweek
cards.body: For much of industrial history, employees routinely labored 60 or more hours each week with no overtime pay. That changed in 1938 when President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Fair Labor Standards Act. Designed during the Great Depression to encourage businesses to hire more workers rather than overwork existing staff, the law introduced the first federal minimum wage at 25 cents an hour and required employers to pay time-and-a-half for hours beyond 40.

sources.title: Wages and the Fair Labor Standards Act

cards.title: The US Income Tax Was Ruled Unconstitutional Before It Was Legal
cards.body: In 1894, Congress enacted a modest peacetime income tax of 2% on incomes exceeding $4,000. Just one year later, in Pollock v. Farmers' Loan & Trust Co., the Supreme Court struck the entire law down, ruling that taxing income from rents and dividends was an unapportioned direct tax forbidden by the Constitution. It took nearly two decades of political warfare and the 1913 ratification of the 16th Amendment to finally make federal income taxation legal.

cards.title: Why More Workers in the Economy Don't Steal Existing Jobs
cards.body: Many people assume an economy contains a fixed amount of work to be done, meaning any new worker—whether an immigrant, a youth, or a retiree—must take a job away from someone else. Economists call this the "lump of labor fallacy." In reality, employment is not a zero-sum game. New workers earn wages and spend them on food, housing, and entertainment, expanding aggregate demand and creating new jobs across the broader economy.

cards.title: How Economists Built the World's Extreme Poverty Line
cards.body: In 1990, World Bank researchers sought a single, objective benchmark to measure extreme global deprivation. Examining national poverty thresholds across the world's poorest nations, they discovered that local lines clustered around roughly $31 a month—about one dollar a day. Adjusted periodically for global inflation and purchasing power, this benchmark was updated to $1.90 in 2015 and $2.15 in 2022, providing the foundation for monitoring global progress against severe poverty.

quizzes.question: What happened to 401(k) participation rates when companies shifted from opt-in to automatic enrollment?
options: Participation stayed virtually the same
Participation surged from 37% to 86%
Participation dropped because workers felt coerced
Participation rose modestly from 37% to 45%
quizzes.explanation: Switching the default setting leveraged human inertia, causing 401(k) sign-up rates among new employees to jump to 86%.

quizzes.question: What was the initial federal minimum wage established by the US Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938?
options: $1.00 per hour
50 cents per hour
25 cents per hour
10 cents per hour
quizzes.explanation: The 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act set America's first federal minimum wage at 25 cents per hour alongside mandatory overtime pay.

quizzes.question: Why did the US need a constitutional amendment in 1913 to create a permanent federal income tax?
options: The Supreme Court had ruled a previous income tax unconstitutional in 1895
The President did not have the authority to sign tax bills
State governments were legally obligated to collect all national revenue
The original Constitution forbade all forms of federal taxation
quizzes.explanation: In Pollock v. Farmers' Loan & Trust Co., the Supreme Court struck down the 1894 income tax, requiring the 16th Amendment to make it constitutional.

quizzes.question: What core misconception defines the economic concept known as the "lump of labor fallacy"?
options: That manual labor is more productive than office work
That an economy has a fixed, static amount of work to be distributed
That higher wages inevitably lead to mass unemployment
That saving money during a recession hurts economic growth
quizzes.explanation: The fallacy assumes the amount of work in an economy is fixed, ignoring that new workers also consume goods and generate new jobs.

quizzes.question: How did World Bank researchers initially determine the global "dollar-a-day" poverty line in 1990?
options: By calculating the cost of a basic food basket in the United States
By averaging national poverty lines across the world's poorest countries
By dividing the global GDP by total world population
By surveying the minimum legal wage across European nations
quizzes.explanation: Researchers analyzed domestic poverty thresholds in very low-income nations and found they clustered around $31 per month, or about $1 a day.

guesses.prompt: What percentage of new hires enrolled in a 401(k) when enrollment was made automatic instead of opt-in?
guesses.explanation: Simply changing the default choice to automatic enrollment boosted 401(k) participation from 37% to 86%.

guesses.prompt: What was the original US federal minimum wage per hour set by the Fair Labor Standards Act in 1938?
guesses.explanation: The 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act set the first federal minimum wage at 25 cents per hour.

misconceptions.claim: The US federal government always had the constitutional authority to tax personal income directly.
misconceptions.explanation: The Supreme Court struck down peacetime federal income taxes in 1895; it took the 16th Amendment in 1913 to make direct income taxation legal.

misconceptions.claim: Allowing more workers into the labor force inevitably deprives existing workers of jobs.
misconceptions.explanation: This is the 'lump of labor fallacy.' New workers earn and spend wages, expanding aggregate economic demand and creating additional employment.
